segments.text: 哈喽大家好 欢迎来到秋时长拉篇课程系列
本次拉篇课程呢 我给大家分析一下南方电网拍的这条短片走在光芒之前
在分析这部短片之前 我先给大家介绍一下这部短片的背景信息
短片的导演呢 叫大赫 圣家北京的CEO和CEO70后 星锐导演
这部短片全片有5分14秒 包含6个大事
分别是大玩区 习电 动送 数字电网 相存振兴 一带一路 知心 输入
这部段片的创作思路使用颠覆传统的那种固定虚实模式
用旬油采封式的风格 为大家呈现了一部不一样的宣传片
那什么是旬油采封式呢
旬油采封式的风格是一种创作的手法
它强调通过油力观察体验的方式
手机和挖掘素材 并以此为基础进行艺术创作
在这种风格下,创造者会像旅游者一样,在不同的地点环境中有走,记录下所见所门,感受当地的分土人情,然后将这些元素融入到视频作品中,时期负有独特的地狱色彩和生活气息。
走在光芒之前,这部宣传片导演大赫和他的团队,深入到了南方电网相关的各个项目和场景中,亲自体验和观察这些项目的时期情况。

career, lack of confidence, fear of judgment, or not trusting my ideas enough to say the least.
For quite some time, I thought I was just doing something wrong. I wondered why there were days
where it was just so hard to do the work, and if I was doing something that I loved to do,
and why I did sometimes working on a project feel like going to more. But I realized
through enough practice and reading and talking with friends about it that these
feelings are truly part of it and the real battle is going against this thing
called resistance. I wish this was something that I learned about earlier, especially
a couple of years ago when I decided to quit my very well-paying 9-5 in order
to start a freelance career. You know, you always hear people say pursue what makes you happy, pursue your passion, and you'll never work a day in your life.
But there I was doing exactly that, and yet I still felt like I was hitting all these internal roadblocks, and it didn't make sense to me as to why.
There was nothing literally standing in my way, except for myself, but it wasn't until
I read this book called The War of Art by Stephen Pressfield that I first heard about
this term and also truly started to understand why I was feeling this way.
We can say resistance takes form as a number of things.
The pressure to fit in, fear of judgment, self-doubt, procrastination, isolation, ridicule,
rejection, humiliation and despair, and overall hell. It's a whole number of
things really that we can spiral down into, but overall most of these things fall
under the umbrella of resistance. We could also think of it as the little
annoying voice in our heads that constantly make us second guess ourselves. It
tells us all these things that we know are not true, but still tries to convince
as otherwise, and it's to keep us, you know, comfortable in our safe bubble. But ironically,
this is the very thing that holds us back from reaching our full potential.
In the beginning, not only did I feel all of those things, I also didn't know it was an actual
thing that a lot of people experienced, and I often thought that the work just came so easily
to everybody else whether it was client work or personal projects or creating videos on YouTube
and it wasn't even the work itself that was hard it was mostly just the process of sitting down
and starting and then to keep going but the more I researched about it the more I realized
that this is a more universal experience than I thought fortunately there is a simple phrase
and reminder get us out of this pit of calamity and despair and it's to give yourself permission.
Ethan Hawke talks about this in his popular TED Talk.
You know a lot of people really struggle to give themselves permission to be creative and
reasonably so I mean we're all a little suspect of our own talent because I think that most of us
really want to offer the world something of quality, something that the world will consider good
or important and that's really the enemy because it's not up to us whether what we do is any good.
We know this the time of our life is so short and how we spend it are we spending it doing what's
important to us most of us not. A huge reason why most people won't pursue their ideas is because
it's easier not to. We live in a world where putting ourselves out there often means the possibility
of being judged or ejected and it's easier to hide altogether. But as the writers and poets
and artists would agree, there's no greater suffering than denying what you're dying to say.
And there's no greater feeling than letting the stories inside you spill out. It's such a simple
thing. Give yourself permission. It's almost absurd because it's basically common sense.
yet on some days it's so difficult and the only thing standing in my way would
be myself. I will say that after learning about resistance that it's easier to
come back from creative slumps than it used to be, but it's definitely still
something that I constantly deal with regular like on a daily basis pretty much.
But like Ethan said, creativity is vital to answer, and who knows, maybe somewhere, somebody has to hear what you have to say.
We're all in a rock and space anyway, so do the thing, give yourself permission, get out of your own way, and don't deny the world of your contribution.
I end up discussing this topic a lot on this channel and with my friends in real life,
because I don't think it's something that we truly get over. I think that
resistance is just something that we get better at dealing with as we get more
experience and as time goes on. But the good thing about it is that I feel like
confidence builds up every time you do get through it. But if this is something
that you relate to and you want to learn more about it, I highly highly recommend
the book The War of Art by Stephen Pressfield. I wish that somebody told me to
read this book earlier. It would have just saved me so much stress and anxiety. It's quite the
popular book so I'm not gonna say too much about it, but if you are interested then I will leave
